paper_metadata.title: Evidence for a phase transition in an AlCrFe2Ni2 high entropy alloy processed by high-pressure torsion

evidence.quote: An as-cast AlCrFe2Ni2 high entropy alloy consisting of face-centered cubic (FCC), ordered body-centered cubic (B2) and body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solution phases was processed by high-pressure torsion (HPT)
the fracture mode of the AlCrFe2Ni2 HEA alloy changes from ductile fracture in the as-cast condition to a mixed character of ductile and quasi-cleavage fracture after HPT processing.

Alloy ingots with nominal compositions of AlCrFe2Ni2 (at%) were prepared by arc-melting a mixture of pure metals having purities above 99.9 wt% in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere on a water-cooled Cu hearth.

In the AlCrFe2Ni2 alloy, the Fe and the Cr-rich FCC solid solution phase have good ductility but low strength whereas the Al and Ni-rich B2 and BCC solid solutions exhibit high strength but poor ductility.
Fe and Cr atoms diffuse from the FCC phase to the B2 and/or BCC phase while the Ni and Al atoms diffuse from the B2 and/or BCC phase to the FCC phase
The BCC and B2 phases are enriched in Ni and Al while the FCC phase is enriched in Fe and Cr .

Under HPT deformation, the high density dislocations continue to grow and accumulate in the FCC phase and the intensified interactions between dislocations result in dislocation entanglements or dislocation jogs which hinder any further movement of dislocations.
The high shear strain in HPT induces a high density of defects, such as dislocations and vacancies, and this reduces the apparent activation energy of diffusion

mechanisms.name: diffusional alloying induced by severe shear strain

evidence.quote: By analogy with the mechanical alloying process, it is proposed that the phase transition driven by HPT is a direct consequence of the severe shear strain which induces diffusional alloying.

The deformation induced transition from B2 and/or the BCC phase to the FCC phase results in solid solution strengthening due to the incorporation of Al atoms with a larger atomic radius within the FCC crystal lattice.
The formation of subgrains, as in the grain refinement, leads to grain boundary strengthening.
This leads to work hardening even though the number of rotations was limited to 1 .
it is reasonable to assume that the introduction of defects and the enhanced diffusion are responsible for the observed phase transition under HPT deformation

the effect of HPT processing on the phase transition is a consequence of the severe shear-induced mechanical mixing which takes place by enhanced diffusion due to the introduction of defects and the reduction of length scale of various phases during the HPT .
the fracture mode of the AlCrFe2Ni2 HEA alloy changes from ductile fracture in the as-cast condition
a ductile and quasi-cleavage mixed fracture mechanism governed the tensile response of the HPT-processed alloys
more tangles of dislocations and fine grains lead to increased microvoid nucleation and this will shorten the critical strain to fracture since coalesence can occur more quickly .
